weak_points.impact: Furniture brought in 9.0K in Sales, but after costs it lost 1.5K overall — every sale here is currently costing more than it earns. Checked this by reshuffling the data thousands of times — it stayed unprofitable every time, not just in this specific sample.
weak_points.suggested_action: Find out whether the losses come from discounting too heavily or from the underlying cost being too high. If it's discounting, capping how much gets discounted here should fix it without losing the sales. If it's cost, that likely needs a price increase or a cheaper way to deliver it.

weak_points.problem: Big discounts are losing money, not just cutting profit
weak_points.impact: Once a discount goes above 41-60%, those sales stop making money entirely and start losing it instead — on average, losing about 9.6% of the sale price for every order discounted that much. Checked this by reshuffling the data thousands of times — this discount band stayed unprofitable every time, not just in this specific sample.
weak_points.suggested_action: Consider capping discounts at around 21-40%, which is the highest level where sales were still profitable. Anything beyond that could require manager approval instead of being offered automatically at checkout.

weak_points.impact: Sales dropped from 15.6K to 8.1K between 2023 and 2024 — a 48.0% decrease. Worth a caveat: reshuffling the data sometimes made this decline disappear, so it's a lead worth checking rather than a confirmed trend.
weak_points.suggested_action: Check whether this drop is happening across the board or mainly in one specific group. If it's just one group, something specific likely changed there and can probably be fixed. If it's happening everywhere at once, the cause is more likely something external.

weak_points.problem: A few unusually high Profit values
weak_points.impact: Just 3 records (1.9% of all rows) have Profit values far above everything else — but together they make up 37.3% of the total. That's enough for a handful of records to make an average or total look bigger than it really is for most of the data. Worth a caveat: reshuffling the data sometimes brought this back under 20%, so how much these records skew things may vary.
weak_points.suggested_action: Take a look at these 3 records specifically. If they're real (a genuinely huge order, an unusually long stay, etc.), that's fine — just know they're skewing the numbers. If they look like typos or data entry mistakes, fixing them will make averages and totals more trustworthy.

weak_points.impact: East brought in 8.1K in Sales, but after costs it lost 209.7 overall — every sale here is currently costing more than it earns. Worth a caveat: reshuffling the data sometimes pushed this back into profit, so the loss may not be as consistent as it looks here.
weak_points.suggested_action: Find out whether the losses come from discounting too heavily or from the underlying cost being too high. If it's discounting, capping how much gets discounted here should fix it without losing the sales. If it's cost, that likely needs a price increase or a cheaper way to deliver it.
